Howard here, founder of Alknoma.

We didn't start with a product. We started with an ANNOYANCE. Agents were impressive while you were talking to them, and then, as soon as you stopped typing, they effectively disappeared.

You'd put one in Slack and end up with another bot sitting in a channel waiting for someone to tell it what to do.

You don't prompt your teammates. [...] A lot of work in a team is essentially waiting.

Waiting isn't failure. It's the norm. And that happens to be one of the things LLM agents are worst at. Ayven reasons about when it should wake up next, EVERY SINGLE TIME, across thousands of runs a week.

It is about recognising a deadline, annual leave, or when a teammate has gone quiet. The async gap is hard to nail down. Ayven does that.

3. What is the base unit of a fact.

In a team, things change constantly. Someone changes their mind, a deadline moves, a customer replies, a meeting gets cancelled. An agent would treat information that was true two days ago as gospel. Change is the critical signal, and that was difficult to implement when teamwork is so unpredictable. Ayven makes sure the right things change with it.

results.content:

minimalist phone: reduce your screentime

@derb12  @rhea\_diamante Hey Rhea, maybe @derb12 didn't receive a notification so I will try to answer: Hunters (especially those well-known in the community) can give some credit to your tool. When other people in the community know them, and even the internal PH team, the product is more likely to be featured and if the hunter has a big following, more people can be notified on the launch day.

Report

Foued Sendi

Great breakdown, Nika. I agree that launching too early can create noise instead of useful feedback.

For a knowledge product like AURELIA, my minimum requirements are slightly different:

– A complete and coherent core framework.

– Clear documentation so people can understand the idea. [...] for a chrome extension outside an app store, the usual split i see: stripe if you want maximum control and don't mind handling eu vat and invoicing yourself, paddle (or lemon squeezy) if you'd rather pay a bit more and have them act as merchant of record so the tax and compliance mess is their problem, not yours. for a solo maker the merchant-of-record route usually saves more headaches than it costs, especially once you sell into the eu.

the one thing i'd decide first, before the tool: onetime vrs subscription. that choice drives which of them fits better more than the brand does.

@varun1jan That's why it should be directly told in the headline what the product does (tho with the limited characters, I think that for PH it is about 30 to 40?)

Matthias Strålman

your list is basically the checklist i've been working through for august 2. the one i'd add, and the one i underestimated most: the app has to be live and the payments actually tested end to end, not just "integrated." a launch-day visitor who can't buy or redeem is traffic you never get back.

where i'd push back gently: i don't think you need a big engaged user base, just enough real users that the day isn't you talking to yourself. for a solo maker that bar is lower than it looks.
